name: Nature trivia (medium)
description: 50 medium questions about animals, plants, weather, ecosystems. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: Which metal in the oxygen-carrying protein haemocyanin gives octopus blood its blue colour?
items.explain: Octopus haemocyanin uses copper to carry oxygen, whereas human haemoglobin uses iron. The copper-based protein is also efficient in cold, low-oxygen water.

source.title: Octopuses keep surprising us - here are eight examples how

items.question: What is the job of two of an octopus's three hearts?
answers: Pumping blood to the arms only
items.explain: Two branchial hearts push blood past the gills to pick up oxygen. The third heart circulates blood around the rest of the body.

source.title: Octopuses keep surprising us - here are eight examples how

items.question: According to NOAA, blue whales are found in all oceans except which one?
items.explain: NOAA states that blue whales occur in all oceans except the Arctic. Their distribution mostly follows where krill are concentrated.

source.title: Blue Whale | NOAA Fisheries

items.question: A blue whale's tongue alone can weigh about as much as which land animal?
items.explain: National Geographic notes that a blue whale's tongue alone can weigh as much as an elephant. The whale uses it to force water out through its baleen plates.

source.title: Blue whale, facts and photos

items.question: When water runs out, a tardigrade curls into a dried-up ball known by what name?
items.explain: In a state called cryptobiosis, a tardigrade curls into a dried ball called a tun and can revive when water returns.

source.title: Tardigrades (Water Bears) - Carleton College SERC

items.question: Although it can grow as tall as many trees, bamboo is botanically a type of what?
items.explain: Bamboo is not technically a tree. It belongs to the grass family and is often called the fastest-growing grass.

source.title: 8 Amazing Bamboo Facts - One Tree Planted

items.question: What must happen before a Venus flytrap snaps its trap shut?
answers: Sweet nectar fills the trap to the brim
Its trigger hairs are touched twice in quick succession
Sunlight strikes the red lining for a full minute
The trap senses body heat from nearby prey
items.correct: Its trigger hairs are touched twice in quick succession
items.explain: The trap closes when an insect trips its trigger hairs twice within a short time. This avoids wasting energy on false alarms such as raindrops.

source.title: How does the Venus flytrap work? - Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

items.question: Which conifer is the tallest tree species on Earth?
items.explain: Britannica describes the coast redwood (Sequoia sempervirens) as the tallest of all living trees. The giant sequoia is bulkier but not as tall.

source.title: Coast redwood | Britannica

items.question: Coast redwoods are native to a narrow strip of the Pacific coast defined by what feature?
items.explain: Britannica says coast redwoods are endemic to the fog belt of the coastal range, from southwestern Oregon to central California.

source.title: Coast redwood | Britannica

items.question: During coral bleaching, corals expel which microscopic partners that normally supply much of their food?
items.explain: High water temperatures make corals lose their zooxanthellae, the algae that produce the food corals need. The tissue then turns nearly transparent, showing the white skeleton.

source.title: Corals and Coral Reefs - Smithsonian Ocean Portal

items.question: Coral polyps build reefs by secreting skeletons made of which compound?
items.explain: Polyps secrete calcium carbonate skeletons. Over time these accumulate into limestone reef structures such as the Great Barrier Reef.

source.title: How do coral polyps build the Great Barrier Reef? | Britannica

items.question: Corals are invertebrates in which animal group, a group characterised by stinging tentacles?
items.explain: The Great Barrier Reef Foundation explains that corals belong to the Cnidaria, animals characterised by stinging tentacles.

source.title: What is coral? - Great Barrier Reef Foundation

items.question: An EF5 tornado on the Enhanced Fujita scale is rated by estimated winds above roughly what speed?
items.explain: The National Weather Service lists EF4 as 166–200 mph, so EF5 covers winds greater than 200 mph.

source.title: Enhanced Fujita Scale - National Weather Service

items.question: Which scientist introduced the original tornado damage scale in 1971, later replaced by an 'Enhanced' version?
items.explain: The Fujita scale was introduced in 1971 by Ted Fujita. The Enhanced Fujita scale later replaced it.

source.title: Enhanced Fujita scale - Wikipedia

items.question: In which type of forest in Mexico do eastern North American monarch butterflies roost for the winter?
items.explain: Eastern monarchs overwinter in oyamel fir forests high in the mountains of central Mexico. The cool microclimate there helps them conserve energy.

source.title: Monarch Butterfly Migration and Overwintering - USDA Forest Service

items.question: Monarch caterpillars depend on which plant as their sole host plant?
items.explain: Monarchs lay their eggs on milkweed, the only plant their caterpillars feed on.

source.title: Monarch Butterfly Migration: Mexico's Top Natural Wonder

items.question: Which seabird makes the longest migration of any bird, flying from the Arctic to wintering grounds off Antarctica?
items.explain: The Smithsonian notes that the Arctic tern has the longest migration of all birds, flying from near the North Pole to waters off Antarctica.

source.title: Arctic Tern - Smithsonian Ocean

items.question: In the honey bee waggle dance, what does the length of the waggle run communicate?
items.explain: A longer waggle run means the food source is farther away. The angle of the run signals the direction.

source.title: The Waggle Dance, Apis Mellifera's (Honey Bee's!) High-Tech Navigation System

items.question: In a mycorrhizal partnership, what do plants give fungi in exchange for phosphorus and other soil nutrients?
items.explain: The core exchange in mycorrhizal symbiosis is sugar made by the plant for phosphorus and other nutrients gathered by the fungus.

source.title: Mycorrhiza

items.question: Sea otters help kelp forests flourish by preying on which kelp-grazing animal?
items.explain: Sea otters are a keystone species. By eating sea urchins they reduce grazing pressure on kelp, so kelp forests thrive.

source.title: A Keystone Species, the Sea Otter, Colonizes Glacier Bay - National Park Service

items.question: Which platypuses carry a venomous spur on each hind leg?
items.explain: Male platypuses have a hollow spur on each hind leg connected to a venom gland. It is likely used in fights between males.

source.title: 10 Fascinating Platypus Facts That Will Surprise You - WWF Australia

items.question: Along with the platypus, which animals are the only living egg-laying mammals?
items.explain: The living monotremes are the platypus and four species of echidna.

source.title: Monotreme - Wikipedia

items.question: What is the term for an axolotl keeping juvenile traits, such as feathery gills, throughout its life?
items.explain: Axolotls stay 'young' for their whole lives, with feathery gills and a tail, a phenomenon called neoteny.

source.title: Axolotl | National Geographic

items.question: Emperor penguins build no nest, so how does the male keep the single egg warm through the Antarctic winter?
answers: He balances it on his feet beneath a belly flap
He buries it in a sheltered snow burrow
He wedges it between rocks at the ice edge
He tucks it into a pit lined with feathers
items.correct: He balances it on his feet beneath a belly flap
items.explain: Emperor penguins do not build nests. The male stands upright and incubates a single egg on top of his feet under a loose fold of abdominal skin.

source.title: Emperor Penguin Facts and Information

items.question: In seahorses, the developing embryos are carried by the male inside which specialised structure?
answers: A gill chamber behind his head
A mouth cavity lined with soft tissue
A brood pouch on his abdomen or tail
A fold of skin along his dorsal fin
items.correct: A brood pouch on his abdomen or tail
items.explain: Male seahorses, not females, incubate the embryos in a specialised structure called a brood pouch, which forms on either the abdomen or the tail.

source.title: Morphology of brood pouch formation in the pot-bellied seahorse Hippocampus abdominalis

items.question: Pando, a giant clonal grove of quaking aspen in Utah, has a name that means what in Latin?
items.explain: Pando is Latin for "I spread". The colony is made of about 47,000 genetically identical stems connected to a vast underground root system.

source.title: Pando: The world's largest tree and heaviest living organism

items.question: A lichen is not a single organism but a partnership between a fungus and which kind of partner?
items.explain: A lichen is the result of a mutualistic symbiosis between a fungus and an alga or cyanobacteria.

source.title: Lichens

items.question: On the Saffir-Simpson scale, hurricanes are classed as 'major' starting at which category?
items.explain: Hurricanes rated Category 3 and higher are known as major hurricanes.

source.title: Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale

items.question: A camel's hump is popularly believed to hold water. What does it actually store?
items.explain: Although commonly believed to store water, a camel's hump actually stores fatty tissue. This fat is a source of nourishment when food is scarce.

source.title: Hump

items.question: Despite its name, the electric eel is actually which type of fish?
items.explain: The electric eel is a South American knifefish and is not a true eel.

source.title: Electric eel

items.question: The reintroduction of which predator to Yellowstone in the 1990s set off a well-studied trophic cascade involving elk and woody plants?
items.explain: After wolves were reintroduced, elk numbers fell and browse plants such as willow and aspen grew taller in some places.

source.title: Trophic cascades in Yellowstone: The first 15 years after wolf reintroduction

items.question: Brood X periodical cicadas spend how many years underground as nymphs before they emerge to mate?
items.explain: Brood X is a regional population of periodical cicadas that have lived underground for 17 years awaiting their emergence to the surface to mate.

source.title: Brood X Cicada Emergence

items.question: During their long years underground, periodical cicada nymphs feed on what?
items.explain: Periodical cicadas in Brood X spend their years underground feeding on juices from tree roots.

source.title: Return of Brood X Cicadas - The National Wildlife Federation Blog

items.question: Pangolins are the only mammals covered in scales. What are those scales made of?
items.explain: Pangolins are the only mammals with scales covering the whole body, and the scales are made of keratin, the same protein as human fingernails.

source.title: Weird and Wonderful Creatures: The Pangolin

items.question: How do the above-ground roots of mangrove trees help reduce coastal erosion?
answers: They draw groundwater away from the shore
They slow water flow so sediment settles
They harden the sand with salty secretions
They break up waves by floating offshore
items.correct: They slow water flow so sediment settles
items.explain: Mangroves' unique above-ground roots slow down water flows and encourage sediment deposits, which reduces coastal erosion.

source.title: Ensuring a Future for Mangroves in the U.S.

items.question: Why can only mosses, lichens and low shrubs grow in the Arctic tundra?
answers: The soil is far too salty
Roots cannot penetrate the frozen soil
Sunlight is absent all year round
items.correct: Roots cannot penetrate the frozen soil
items.explain: Roots can't penetrate the frozen soil, so only moss, lichen, and low shrubs can grow there.

source.title: Tundra and Permafrost

items.question: Which layer of a tropical rainforest is home to an estimated 70 to 90 percent of the forest's species?
items.explain: An estimated 70-90% of all rainforest species live in the canopy, making it the most biodiverse part of the rainforest.

source.title: Rainforest Biodiversity: Layer by Layer - Population Education

items.question: Bats use echolocation to hunt in the dark. In which range of sound do they call?
answers: Seismic thumps sent through the ground
items.explain: Bats produce sound waves at frequencies above human hearing, called ultrasound, and these waves bounce off objects in their environment.

source.title: Echolocation - Bats (U.S. National Park Service)

items.question: How do dolphins manage to rest while still surfacing to breathe?
answers: By sleeping only in tidal shallows
By floating motionless for hours at depth
By dropping their metabolism into torpor
By resting one half of the brain at a time
items.correct: By resting one half of the brain at a time
items.explain: Dolphins use unihemispheric sleep, shutting down half the brain at a time, which is thought to have evolved so they can breathe at the surface even while snoozing.

source.title: Dolphins Sleep With Only Half Their Brain at a Time

items.question: A giraffe's very long neck contains how many vertebrae, the same number found in a mouse's neck?
items.explain: Almost all mammals have seven neck vertebrae. A giraffe's are simply stretched out to enormous length.

source.title: How is a mouse like a giraffe? - Natural History Museum

items.question: What is the long, spiralling 'tusk' of a male narwhal actually?
items.explain: The tusk is an enlarged tooth that grows through the upper lip and has many nerve endings. It is not a horn.

source.title: Unicorn of the Sea: Fascinating Narwhal Facts - WWF

items.question: Which type of cloud, often topped with an anvil shape, is the classic thunderstorm cloud?
items.explain: Cumulonimbus clouds grow tall, and winds flatten their tops into an anvil shape. They bring heavy rain, hail and lightning.

source.title: Cumulonimbus clouds - UCAR Center for Science Education

items.question: El Niño is a climate pattern marked by unusual warming of ocean surface waters in which region?
answers: The central and eastern tropical Pacific
items.correct: The central and eastern tropical Pacific
items.explain: NOAA describes El Niño as warming of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean. This warming can shift weather patterns worldwide.

source.title: Understanding El Niño & ENSO - NOAA

items.question: The titan arum, famous as the 'corpse flower' for its stench, is native to the rainforests of which Indonesian island?
items.explain: The titan arum (Amorphophallus titanum) is native to the tropical forests of Sumatra in Indonesia.

source.title: Corpse Flower - Missouri Botanical Garden

items.question: Which pigments, present in leaves all summer but masked by chlorophyll, give autumn leaves their yellow and orange colours?
items.explain: Carotenoids are in the leaf all season and show through once the green chlorophyll breaks down. Red anthocyanins, by contrast, are mostly made in autumn.

source.title: Science of Fall Colors - USDA Forest Service

items.question: Which forest biome, dominated by conifers such as pines, spruces and larches, is the world's largest?
items.explain: The taiga, or boreal forest, forms a vast belt across the northern latitudes. It covers roughly 11.5% of Earth's land area.

source.title: Taiga - Wikipedia

items.question: Where do brightly coloured wild poison dart frogs get the toxins in their skin?
answers: From the ants and mites they eat
From venom glands they grow as adults
From bacteria living on their skin
From poisonous plant sap they lick
items.correct: From the ants and mites they eat
items.explain: The frogs absorb alkaloids from the ants, mites and other small prey they eat. That is why frogs raised in captivity on other diets are not poisonous.

source.title: Poison Frogs - Los Angeles Zoo and Botanical Gardens

items.question: By area, which place is the largest desert on Earth?
items.explain: A desert is defined by low precipitation, not heat. Antarctica covers about 14.2 million square kilometres, which is bigger than the Sahara.

source.title: The world's largest desert is enormous and there's hardly any rain - BBC Discover Wildlife

items.question: Beavers are called 'ecosystem engineers' because their dams turn streams into what kind of habitat?
answers: Fast rapids that oxygenate the water
Dry meadows with deep, rich soil
items.explain: Beaver dams slow the water and create ponds and wetlands. These give habitat to many other animals and plants and help clean the water.

source.title: Beaver - WWF

items.question: Which group of small birds is noted as the only one able to fly backwards?
items.explain: Hummingbirds can hover and fly backwards, which lets them position themselves at flowers. Their wing joints and figure-eight wing stroke make this possible.

source.title: Interesting Facts on Hummingbirds - UC Davis Hummingbird Health and Conservation Program
